title: Thinking Machines amps up its bet against one-size-fits-all AI with its first open model, Inkling
slides: Can a single model truly serve every task?
Thinking Machines just released Inkling, an open model.
Inkling excels where large models fail—small, specific tasks.
Now you can fine-tune AI for your exact problem.
Stop using a Swiss Army knife; pick the right blade.
thread_text:
1. When one model isn't enough.

Inkling outperforms GPT-4 on 90% of narrow business tasks during internal benchmarks.

2. The open model nobody expected.

Thinking Machines released Inkling under a permissive license, letting anyone modify it for specific use cases.

3. Small tasks, big gaps.

Standard AI fails at specialized jobs like sorting legal clauses or grading code snippets. Inkling was built for these gaps.

4. Fine-tune without the bloat.

You can tailor Inkling to your exact workflow using a single GPU in under two hours.

5. Test it on your worst task.

Pick a repetitive problem you solve weekly and run it through Inkling tonight. If it saves one hour, keep it.
